attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as router between lan-a (192.168.10.0/24, node2) and lan-b (192.168.20.0/24, node3) using previously-unassigned vtnet1/vtnet2 as opt1/opt2. Added firewall pass rules for both segments and a hybrid-mode outbound NAT rule that SNATs only lan-a→lan-b traffic to node1's opt2 address (192.168.20.1), leaving lan-b→lan-a traffic unmodified. Verified via tcpdump on node1's interfaces that node2→node3 traffic arrives at node3 sourced from 192.168.20.1, while node3→node2 traffic still arrives sourced from node3's real address (192.168.20.2). Completed the mandatory restart protocol on all three nodes: captured healthy baselines, restarted each node one at a time via native reboot, confirmed changed boot identity (boot_id for the RHEL nodes, kern.boottime for the FreeBSD/OPNsense router), and re-verified the asymmetric NAT behavior end-to-end after all three restarts.
